title: Improving guideline adherence in physiotherapy for hip and knee osteoarthritis: development and evaluation of a tailored implementation intervention
summary:
Osteoarthritis is a highly prevalent disease and a leading cause of pain and disability in older adults. Weight-bearing joints, such as the knees and hips, are particularly frequently affected. Clinical practice guidelines systematically summarise current scientific evidence on various therapeutic approaches and are intended to support healthcare professionals and patients in making informed decisions to achieve optimal care. However, implementing guideline recommendations into physiotherapy practice remains challenging.

The aim of the study is to develop and evaluate a tailored implemenation intervention to enhance the uptake of guideline recommendations in physiotherapy care for patients with hip and knee osteoarthritis.

The implementation intervention will be developed in collaboration with relevant stakeholders (e.g. physiotherapists, patients, receptionists, practice owners). Subsequently, it will be evaluated with regard to its feasibility in clinical practice and its potential to improve the quality of care. To identify potential changes in clinical practice, physiotherapists will complete treatment documentations and questionnaires. In addition, patient-reported outcomes will be assessed.

interventions.name: Tailored implementation intervention (the type and content of the intervention will be developed in collaboration with key stakeholders through focus group discussions)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Physiotherapists: regular treatment of patients diagnosed with hip and/or knee osteoarthritis

Patients: a clinical diagnosis of hip and/or knee osteoarthritis confirmed by a physician, and a medical prescription for physiotherapy management
Exclusion criteria:
Physiotherapists: none

Patients: osteoarthritis due to acute traumatic events (e.g. fractures, accidents); planned operations on the affected joint during the study period; comorbidities that restrict participation in physiotherapy (e.g. severe cardiovascular diseases, neurological diseases)
